one_line: Controlled WebMCP-to-desktop bridge for observing, approving, executing, and verifying screen workflows.
what_it_does: Lense exposes structured tools and a bounded local companion so an agent can observe screens, propose actions, obtain approval, execute desktop input, verify results, and log the workflow.
leverage_rationale: The structured observe-propose-approve-act-verify loop and shared event state extend WebMCP beyond webpages into otherwise inaccessible desktop software; generic UI-driving agents would be materially less bounded and verifiable.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly combines WebMCP, screen observation, explicit approvals, verification, event log, and optional local desktop bridge.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows a Woodcutting lab with a control panel for what Lense should do and verification-oriented controls.
Frame sheets show changing application state across a multi-step desktop/browser workflow.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent control loop and multiple demonstrations, but the submitted packet has no transcript and the frame sheets are low-resolution, so end-to-end completion and robustness are only partially evidenced.
execution_evidence: About text names deterministic Paint, Notepad, and Claims demonstrations.
Frames show persistent controls and evolving task state.
Devpost page provides a prominent demo video thumbnail.
impact_rationale: A broad, credible audience needs safe agent assistance for legacy and desktop software; approvals and post-action verification address a real safety and reliability gap.
impact_evidence: About text identifies desktop, legacy enterprise, creative, testing, and operating-system interfaces as targets.
Observe → Propose → Approve → Act → Verify is clearly articulated.
creativity_rationale: Treating WebMCP as a controlled plane for non-web software, with screen observation and explicit human authorization, is a memorable and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Concept explicitly asks what happens when WebMCP reaches beyond the webpage.
Bounded local companion plus inspectable event timeline is an unusual extension of WebMCP.
usability_note: The approval-and-verification model is understandable, though the desktop bridge and setup add friction.
red_flags: No transcript; visual text is small and the full agent invocation is not directly legible.
standouts: Strong security boundary and verification framing for desktop control.
advance_reason: High leverage and originality with credible product evidence; execution merits deeper validation.

one_line: Human-approved WebMCP assistant for inspecting, comparing, cleaning, and exporting business datasets.
what_it_does: DataBridge exposes dataset inspection, duplicate/missing-field/anomaly detection, comparison, price analysis, action planning, and approval-gated clean export.
leverage_rationale: Structured dataset operations and a local approval gate make agent work more reliable than UI driving, but the core analysis is a familiar capability that remains possible with other agent interfaces.
leverage_evidence: Eight named structured tools cover inspection through export.
Export is explicitly protected by human approval and source data remains unchanged.
Demo screenshot visibly shows Agent activity and inspect_dataset/export_clean_data entries.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and the packaging shows a usable activity trail, but low-resolution frame sheets do not establish every analysis path or successful export end to end.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows the agent activity interface and tool-call history.
Frames show dashboard/list/detail workflow and DataBridge AI Agent configuration.
About text describes a complete set of operations.
impact_rationale: Fragmented business data and safe cleaning are common, concrete problems; the workflow offers practical diagnostic and action-planning value while avoiding silent mutation.
impact_evidence: Description names CSV, supplier, inventory, purchase, and disconnected data sources.
Duplicate, missing-field, anomaly, comparison, and price-change workflows are directly relevant.
creativity_rationale: This is a competent data-agent application with a solid approval/audit angle, but the underlying category and interaction are established.
creativity_evidence: Combines multiple business-data diagnostics with an approval-gated export.
WebMCP tool activity is made visible and auditable.
usability_note: The staged workflow and activity trail suggest good explainability, though setup and data loading may add friction.
red_flags: No transcript and no direct evidence of all eight operations completing.
standouts: Clear safety boundary around clean-data export.
advance_reason: Strong practical fit and credible tool-use evidence, though novelty and end-to-end proof are moderate.

one_line: Parametric 3D vessel editor that turns agent-directed shapes into deterministic printable clay templates.
what_it_does: Unfolded lets humans and agents edit vessel parameters, synchronizes paired browsers, supports undo/redo, and exports geometry-faithful multipage templates.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP supplies structured parameter control while the application deterministically computes geometry and export; this sharply improves precision and repeatability over an agent attempting to generate PDFs directly.
leverage_evidence: Transcript explains the agent sends parameters while the app generates precise matching templates.
Video visibly shows a faceted vessel beside technical/template geometry and Export control.
About text emphasizes deterministic multipage PDF output and reversible human/agent changes.
execution_rationale: The live 179-second demo and transcript show pairing, agent-driven update, synchronization, and undo/redo; the packet supports a strong central workflow, with some export details only visually implied.
execution_evidence: Transcript describes paired browser synchronization in under one second and shows an agent change arriving.
Frames show 3D vessel and corresponding outline/template views.
Devpost packaging visibly labels the parametric 3D editor and WebMCP demo.
impact_rationale: Potters have a specific costly failure mode—misaligned handmade templates—and deterministic printable geometry directly reduces wasted studio time and material.
impact_evidence: About text describes cereal-box template practice and failures discovered after hours of building.
Output is explicitly a multipage PDF true to the built 3D shape.
creativity_rationale: The human-agent division of labor—agent handles complex shape reasoning while a parametric editor guarantees fabrication geometry—is an original, deeply pursued use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Connects conversational shape changes to a reversible parametric editor and physical craft workflow.
Includes paired-browser synchronization rather than merely generating an image.
usability_note: Direct parameter editing, pairing, and undo/redo support collaboration, though pairing adds setup.
red_flags: Physical fabrication success is claimed rather than independently observed in the packet.
standouts: Excellent deterministic handoff from agent intent to buildable geometry.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage, impact, and demonstrated creative human-agent collaboration.

one_line: Agent-assisted travel planner that searches, budgets, replans, and stages bookings with traveler approval.
what_it_does: Arion turns natural-language travel requests into map-backed itineraries, searches flights/stays/activities/vehicles, balances constraints, and gates booking/payment.
leverage_rationale: Structured search, itinerary, budget, shortlist, and replanning tools reduce cross-site friction, but a general agent could achieve much of the same outcome with UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text names structured tools for searching options, creating itineraries, saving shortlists, checking budgets, and replanning.
Screenshot visibly shows map, budget, itinerary, trip assistant, and approval-oriented feasibility content.
execution_rationale: The screenshot shows a coherent planning dashboard and substantial itinerary state, but there are no frame sheets or video transcript and no demonstrated booking completion.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows a populated map/planning interface with dates, budget, itinerary, and assistant.
About text describes provider adapters and approval points.
impact_rationale: Travelers face genuine fragmentation across research, comparison, scheduling, and booking; a flexible planner that preserves approval can provide credible value.
impact_evidence: Description identifies the full planning loop and traveler control.
Screenshot shows concrete itinerary, budget, map, and feasibility checks.
creativity_rationale: The synthesis of adaptive itinerary planning, normalized provider data, and safe agent-mediated booking is fresh for a hackathon, though the category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Replanning under changed constraints and explicit booking/payment approval are central features.
usability_note: The map, itinerary, budget, and assistant views make the planning state legible; provider coverage and booking handoff remain unclear.
red_flags: No submitted frame sheets or video transcript; booking/payment path is not demonstrated.
advance_reason: Clear audience and credible planning product, but evidence limits execution and leverage confidence.

one_line: Human-agent 2D room planner with spatial constraints, furniture placement, validation, variants, and undo.
what_it_does: RoomCraft exposes room geometry and furniture state to agents, enabling edits and validation while people review and adjust an actual floor plan.
leverage_rationale: Structured dimensions, object positions, and constraints let agents make precise edits and validate spatial feasibility instead of guessing from images; generic UI driving is materially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: About text lists tools for dimensions, doors, windows, furniture, placement, and validation.
Screenshot visibly shows a 2D floor-plan editor with furniture and measurements.
Claims shared update/history system, variants, and undo.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and the frame sheet shows dashboard-to-detail workflow, but exact collision/door/walking-space validation is not legible and there is no transcript.
execution_evidence: Frames show an interactive editor with changing structured layouts.
Devpost screenshot shows room floor plan, furniture, measurements, and AI conversation.
About text specifies overlap/outside-room/door/walking-space checks.
impact_rationale: Room planning is a concrete need for homeowners, renters, and designers; an editable, constraint-aware plan addresses shortcomings of image generation.
impact_evidence: About text contrasts manual room planners and non-editable image generators.
Visible floor plan includes furniture and spatial dimensions.
creativity_rationale: The actual-floor-plan distinction and human-agent spatial collaboration are a strong new angle on room design, though the general category is known.
creativity_evidence: Agent edits geometry/state rather than generating a decorative room image.
Constraint checking and shared history deepen the interaction model.
usability_note: Visual canvas plus direct manipulation, validation, variants, and undo should support approachable collaboration.
red_flags: No transcript and small frame text prevents checking detailed validation results.
standouts: Strong distinction between editable floor plans and image-only room generation.
advance_reason: Practical, well-scoped human-agent design tool with meaningful structured-state leverage.

one_line: Privacy-first decision workspace where agents search confidential local PDFs but need approval to read pages.
what_it_does: Consensus parses PDFs locally, supports agent search and approval-gated page release, and organizes vendor evidence into a scored decision matrix.
leverage_rationale: The privacy boundary changes what an agent can safely do: structured search without exposing document text, followed by human release, is not comparably achievable through ordinary cloud-agent UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly says confidential PDFs stay local and the agent cannot read pages without approval.
Screenshot shows Evidence vault, vendor matrix, criteria, registered tools, and tool calls.
Frame sheets show a transition from document/decision workspace to populated structured results.
execution_rationale: The concept, evidence vault, matrix, and approval workflow are coherent and visibly packaged, but the packet does not show a full search-to-approved-page-to-cited-answer run.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot visibly shows vendor comparison, evidence vault, and tool-call areas.
About text specifies local parsing, search, and explicit release.
Frames show populated decision workspace states.
impact_rationale: Security, procurement, and legal teams have a specific high-stakes need to search NDA-bound documents without prohibited uploads; the solution directly addresses that contradiction.
impact_evidence: About text identifies SOC 2 reports, DPAs, pricing annexes, and questionnaires under NDA.
Visible matrix criteria include price, SOC 2, data residency, and integrations.
creativity_rationale: The interaction model—agent retrieval over unreadable-to-agent confidential documents with deliberate human release—is novel, memorable, and deeply aligned to the medium.
creativity_evidence: Core pitch reverses the usual document-agent model: find without read access.
Combines privacy boundary, evidence vault, decision matrix, and approval workflow.
usability_note: The matrix and evidence workflow are legible, but approval/release steps may add friction by design.
red_flags: No transcript and no direct proof of the confidential-page release completing end to end.
standouts: Exceptional privacy/usefulness tradeoff handled as the core product interaction.
advance_reason: One of the strongest concepts: transformative leverage and high-stakes, specific audience value.

one_line: Browser-first verifier for cryptographic evidence records, chronology, assertions, and local-file matches.
what_it_does: UCE Evidence Lens exposes read-only WebMCP tools that verify signed public records, distinguish claims from independently checked facts, inspect chronology/rights, and compare local files.
leverage_rationale: Structured, source-bound verification results preserve evidentiary boundaries that a general agent scraping UI could easily collapse; read-only shared state improves precision and trust.
leverage_evidence: About text names seven typed read-only tools and structured source-bound results.
Screenshot visibly lists discovery tools such as verify_uce_record, chronology inspection, assertions, rights, and local-file comparison.
Frames show Native WebMCP discovery, 7 tools discovered, native agent verification, and structured result.
execution_rationale: The production-oriented interface and repeated discovery/verification/structured-result states are coherent and detailed, though exact cryptographic outcomes are not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show open evidence record, verification checks, compare-local-file, and structured result stages.
Devpost screenshot identifies live production tab and named read-only tools.
About text specifies schema, identity, ES256, signature, and chronology checks.
impact_rationale: Creators, agencies, counsel, journalists, and reviewers have a real need to inspect public evidence without confusing assertions with verified facts.
impact_evidence: About text names concrete audiences and evidentiary failure modes.
Verification interface visibly separates record/check workflows.
creativity_rationale: The emphasis on evidentiary boundaries—especially separating claimed dates and assertions from independently checked facts—is an original and technically ambitious agent interaction.
creativity_evidence: Read-only native verification surface with structured results.
Product verifies itself through an independently checkable UCE record, per the submission text.
usability_note: Read-only checks and structured results support trust, though evidence formats and cryptographic terminology may challenge general users.
red_flags: Visual text is small; independent verification of actual signature/chronology values is not possible from the packet.
standouts: Strong provenance-aware distinction between facts, publisher reports, and assertions.
advance_reason: Technically distinctive, evidence-rich, and highly aligned with structured agent capabilities.

one_line: Research board that gathers Reddit discussion, lets users pin/reject sources, and leaves trust decisions to humans.
what_it_does: VibeCheck searches and organizes real-user discussion into claims and source clusters while preserving live human decisions about which sources to trust.
leverage_rationale: The product makes shared source state—pinned/rejected sources and live board context—available to the agent during research, beyond a one-off summary; ordinary browsing can approximate it with more friction.
leverage_evidence: About text explicitly describes rejecting sources and pinning comments during an agent conversation.
Screenshot shows query field, claim cards, and Reddit/forum source panel.
Frames show initial prompt, loading, and populated evidence/result states.
execution_rationale: The search-to-results flow is visibly represented with a coherent interface and populated claims, but source retrieval quality and complete agent invocation are not directly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Frames show input, loading placeholders, generated result cards, and related-source panel.
Devpost screenshot shows RTX 5090 claim cards and source clusters.
About text describes live shared board state.
impact_rationale: Consumers making purchase or technology choices commonly seek authentic user experience beyond marketing; aggregating discussion while preserving human trust decisions is credible value.
impact_evidence: Pitch and about text identify product decisions and Reddit research behavior.
Visible claim cards and source panel concretize the use case.
creativity_rationale: Treating trust judgments—pinning and rejecting sources—as shared live state rather than outsourcing recommendation is a fresh interaction model.
creativity_evidence: About text explicitly rejects becoming another recommendation engine.
Human decides who to believe while agent performs reading and organization.
usability_note: The simple question-to-board flow is approachable; source quality and information density may require careful review.
red_flags: No transcript and no direct visible tool-call sequence; third-party source quality remains a risk.
standouts: Human trust decisions are modeled as live shared state rather than hidden model judgment.
advance_reason: Strong audience fit and notably original collaborative research interaction.

one_line: Benchmark harness measuring DOM-driving versus WebMCP agent performance with a React integration layer.
what_it_does: AgentPerf runs identical tasks through DOM and WebMCP lanes, reporting wall-clock, tokens, round-trips, and success rates, and ships reusable React primitives.
leverage_rationale: The product directly measures and operationalizes the agent-surface delta, while the harness and structured lane isolate what WebMCP changes; the React layer makes adoption repeatable.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies identical prompt/model/verification and DOM versus WebMCP runs.
Benchmark claims 2.4x on a small page and 13.8x on a realistic catalog, with 100% success in both lanes.
Frames visibly show same-page/same-model/same-task comparisons, token counts, charts, and a 13.8x result.
execution_rationale: The scope is unusually complete for a benchmark: CLI, React primitives, two instrumented pages, repeated runs, metrics, and caveats are presented coherently; exact reproducibility is not independently exercised here.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows validation/schema-gating demo with rejected invalid inputs.
Frames show benchmark cards, page-specific comparisons, and increasing DOM versus stable WebMCP counts.
About text lists CLI metrics and n=5 methodology.
impact_rationale: Frontend teams need credible evidence before maintaining an agent surface; a page-sensitive harness can prevent misleading universal performance claims and guide engineering investment.
impact_evidence: About text frames the practical question of what teams get from a second agent surface.
Benchmark reports wall-clock, tokens, round-trips, and success rather than a single headline.
creativity_rationale: Turning a widely repeated but underspecified WebMCP claim into a reproducible, caveated measurement product is a thoughtful and original challenge response.
creativity_evidence: Explicit thesis that the gap belongs to the page, not universally to WebMCP.
Ships a harness rather than only reporting a headline.
usability_note: CLI and React primitives target developers directly, though benchmark setup likely requires technical expertise.
red_flags: Claims are self-reported and the packet does not independently reproduce benchmark runs.
standouts: Excellent methodological caveat and page-sensitive comparison.
advance_reason: Strong execution and evidence with unusually clear WebMCP measurement value.

one_line: AI-assisted visual database schema designer with conversational building, consistency checks, refactoring, and ORM export.
what_it_does: Edaad lets an agent manipulate a real-time schema canvas from natural language, check consistency, refactor safely, and export Prisma ORM definitions.
leverage_rationale: Structured canvas manipulation and schema validation make agent edits more precise than typing SQL, but a general agent with UI access could plausibly achieve much of the same result.
leverage_evidence: About text contrasts SQL suggestions with direct real-time visual canvas manipulation.
Screenshot visibly shows schema designer branding and Templates/Import/Export/ER View controls.

execution_rationale: The product concept and interface are coherent, but there are no video frames and only a video thumbnail/description, limiting credit for completed conversational build, checks, and export.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows the named app and a ChatGPT-to-canvas workflow.
About text lists schema building, consistency checks, refactoring, and Prisma export.
Live demo is reported alive, but no direct run evidence is included.
impact_rationale: Developers and teams benefit from turning natural-language requirements into inspectable schemas and exports, though the audience/problem fit is less differentiated than the strongest submissions.
impact_evidence: Description identifies conversational schema building and safe refactoring.
Visible product includes ER View and export controls.
creativity_rationale: Direct agent manipulation of a visual database canvas with consistency-aware refactoring is a fresh synthesis, though schema design tools and AI code generation are established.
creativity_evidence: Moves from text SQL suggestion to a real-time visual schema artifact.
Combines conversational construction with soft-delete consistency checks and ORM export.
usability_note: Visual ER editing and export are familiar affordances; conversational setup may reduce schema-authoring friction.
red_flags: No submitted frame sheets; central workflow and export are not independently visible end to end.
